title: 1985 AHSME Problem 24
statement: A non-zero digit is chosen in such a way that the probability of choosing digit \(d\) is \(\log_{10}(d+1)-\log_{10}d.\) The probability that the digit \(2\) is chosen is exactly \(\frac{1}{2}\) the probability that the digit chosen is in the set

solutions.text:
The probability of \(2\) is \(\log_{10}(\frac{3}{2}),\) so twice that probability is \(\log_{10}(\frac{9}{4}).\) For the digits \(4\) through \(8,\) the sum telescopes: \[ \begin{aligned} &\sum_{d=4}^{8} \bigl(\log_{10}(d+1)\\ &\qquad{}-\log_{10}d\bigr) =\log_{10}\frac94. \end{aligned} \] Therefore that set has exactly twice the probability of digit \(2.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Twice the probability of digit \(2\) is \(2\log_{10}(\frac{3}{2})\)
